clue.text: Pages I forgot to add, putting book cover first

indicators.note: putting ... first says the book and cover pieces go ahead of the postscript

parts.note: lee means shelter or cover, as in the lee of a wall
PS, a postscript, is what you write when you forgot to add something to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone tidying a letter adds forgotten pages and puts the book's cover on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pages' is a verb: a pager bleeps you. The three pieces read in answer order once 'putting ... first' moves the book and its cover ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone on a pager is to send them a beep, so pages means bleeps.

clue.text: Late second child

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a ward is a child in someone's legal care

explanation.surface: A second child arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the verb, to support.
explanation.definitionFit: Backward describes a child slow or late in developing.

clue.text: Rehab frequently upset Dr Strange — it's in his head

indicators.note: frequently picks every other letter of Rehab
upset in a down clue turns the word over, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: Repeated rehab disturbs the Marvel sorcerer Dr Strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequently' takes EA from Rehab; 'upset' turns DR to RD.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanum sits inside the ear, part of anyone's head.

clue.text: Withdrawn detective quietly necking drink as expected

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
necking means downing, so the quiet letter comes after the drink it swallows

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A reserved detective quietly downs a drink, just as everyone expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' reverses DET + CIDER + P to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something predicted was foreseen, so it turns out as expected.

clue.text: Credited writer, boring these days

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the writer goes inside the other piece

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A writer gets credit even though these days he is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' but tells you SCRIBE drills into AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe a work to someone is to credit them with it.

clue.text: Actress Winona's raving about one who worked on Gravity

indicators.note: raving about means going wild, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gossip column has the actress Winona Ryder raving about the film Gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' looks like the 2013 space film; rearrange ACTRESS WINONA plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation.

clue.text: Tucking into port, at 16:59?

indicators.note: tucking into means putting inside, so the small word goes inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Eating in a port at one minute to five.
explanation.walkthrough: '16:59' looks like a time, but it is a proportion: sixteen to fifty-nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Two numbers set against each other with a colon express a proportion.

clue.text: Hat worn by southern Gascon

indicators.note: worn by means around, so the hat encloses the other letter

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat

explanation.surface: A man from southern Gascony wears a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascons were famed for bragging, hence 'gasconade' for boasting talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A gascon in lower case is a braggart, from the supposed bluster of people from Gascony.

clue.text: Frames in hand, Ronnie O'Sullivan lost? Prune!

indicators.note: lost means astray, so the gathered letters are jumbled
frames picks the first and last letters of each word, the letters round each word's edge

explanation.surface: Snooker champion Ronnie O'Sullivan loses with frames in hand and is told to cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frames' looks like snooker, but it takes HD, RE and ON from the outer letters of 'hand', 'Ronnie' and 'O'Sullivan'; 'lost' jumbles them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehorn a tree is to cut back its branches severely.

clue.text: Order for ham at the Savoy?

definitions.text: Order for ham at the Savoy?

parts.words: Order for ham at the Savoy?
parts.note: reads like a request for gammon at the Savoy hotel, but ham is a bad actor and the Savoy is also a London theatre, so the order is a script's instruction to a performer

explanation.surface: A diner orders ham at the posh Savoy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is both a grand London hotel and a theatre; 'ham' is an over-acting actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A script's instruction tells an actor where to move or how to act on the boards.

clue.text: What was Jesus Christ Superstar singer's name?

definitions.text: What was Jesus Christ Superstar singer's name?

parts.words: What was Jesus Christ Superstar singer's name?
parts.note: Jesus worked with wood in Nazareth, and Karen of the duo who recorded the song Superstar shared that trade's name as her surname

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking the name of a singer from the musical Jesus Christ Superstar.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical title is a red herring: split it as 'What was Jesus' (his trade) and the singer of the 1971 hit Superstar, Karen of the Carpenters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus followed Joseph's woodworking trade, and Karen and Richard recorded as the Carpenters.

clue.text: Make time for Queen show

indicators.note: time for Queen means the time letter replaces the queen letter

parts.note: to make a place is to reach it
R, for Regina, is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Someone is told to find time to put on a show for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R of REACH for T.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone how to do something is to instruct them.

clue.text: Fading inspector finally probes tip-off …

indicators.note: probes means pushes into, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: waning means fading or declining

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of inspector

explanation.surface: An inspector whose career is waning finally investigates an anonymous tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R, the last letter of 'inspector', and 'probes' sets it inside WANING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is an advance alert or caution about something coming.

clue.text: … in Morse, signal for killer?

parts.note: three dots in Morse code stand for the letter S
a hooter is a horn used to sound a signal

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, Inspector Morse picks up a sign pointing to the murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 12 across, but it is also three dots, which is S in Morse code.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooter is one who fires a gun, so a killer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Brief review of Countdown

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking again from the other end, says the word is read backwards

parts.note: a timer counts down the time remaining

explanation.surface: A short review of the TV quiz show Countdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countdown' looks like the British TV words-and-numbers quiz, but it means TIMER, which 'review of' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the brief or set of instructions defining someone's job.

clue.text: Did Express back serious-looking artist in exile

indicators.note: back says the words just before it are read in reverse order

parts.note: said means did express in words
PO, from po-faced, means looking solemn and disapproving
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper ran a story on a solemn artist living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the newspaper, but 'Did Express' is SAID, which 'back' turns to DIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people scattered away from their homeland, living in exile.

clue.text: Pound put away by Buddy before depression

indicators.note: before says the friend goes ahead of the depression

parts.note: a pal is a buddy or friend
a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Buddy pockets a pound before falling into depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' is a verb, as a heart pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that palpitates throbs or pounds rapidly.

clue.text: Show return, investing in change

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so these letters sit within the coins

parts.note: pence are small change
RET is an abbreviation for return

explanation.surface: A show's takings come back and are invested in loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' is the abbreviation seen on rail tickets; 'investing in' wraps the coins round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show or display put on to deceive.

clue.text: Framework with squares from crossword club

parts.note: the grid is the pattern of squares of a crossword
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A frame of squares taken from a crossword club's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a grating of bars forming squares, and an American football field marked in lines.

clue.text: Fan earned the heart of Chris Pratt

indicators.note: the heart of picks the central letter of Chris
fan means spread out, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A fan wins the heart of the Hollywood actor Chris Pratt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an admirer but is the scramble signal. 'Prat', old slang for the buttocks, is spelt here like the actor's surname for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is old slang for the buttocks, the bottom or behind.

clue.text: North face of Everest traversed by fancy soloist

indicators.note: traversed by means crossed through by, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: Fancy! and Lor! are both old exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: face of picks the opening letter of Everest

explanation.surface: A lone climber crosses the north face of Everest in a fancy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is the exclamation 'Fancy (that)!', which is LOR; N and E, the first letter of 'Everest', go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner prefers to be alone, much as a soloist performs alone.

clue.text: Tipped roast onto family's table linen

indicators.note: tipped means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to pan a show is to roast it with harsh criticism
kin's means the family's

explanation.surface: The roast is tipped on to the family's tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' is a harsh review, PAN, which 'Tipped' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviettes are linen squares used at the table.

clue.text: Alice gets Mad Hatter's last pastry

indicators.note: mad means wild, so these letters are jumbled
last picks the final letter of Hatter's before the possessive

explanation.surface: Alice gets the Mad Hatter's last cake at the tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks part of the Mad Hatter but scrambles ALICE; 'last' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux bun filled with cream.

clue.text: Model's quality nude pics

definitions.note: Model's here reads as model is, the definition then the link

parts.note: class means quality or excellence

indicators.note: nude means stripped, so the word pics loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A model's standing is boosted by tasteful nude photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nude' strips PICS of its first and last letters, leaving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work held up as a standard or exemplar.

clue.text: Will Smith's content to leave everyone behind

indicators.note: behind says everyone comes after the remains of Smith
content to leave means the inner letters of Smith go

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Will Smith is happy to leave everyone behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will Smith' is the actor, but 'Will' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shall and will both form the future tense.

clue.text: Dog, cat, bird?

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
bird and pet are both affectionate terms for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A question listing three animals as if asking which is the odd one out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a flogging whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slim, fast breed of racing hound.

clue.text: Ground sugarcane racehorse partially regurgitated

indicators.note: regurgitated says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A racehorse at the ground brings up some of the sugarcane it has eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes ANERA from 'sugarcane racehorse' and 'regurgitated' brings it back up reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sports ground or stadium.

clue.text: Sit in a loo to change in privacy

indicators.note: to change means the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Retreating to the toilet to get changed in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges the letters of SIT IN A LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is being kept apart from others, a state of seclusion.

clue.text: Suggestive act inspired by Relax

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in by, so the act goes inside the other word

parts.note: to relent is to relax or ease off
do means act or perform

explanation.surface: A racy performance inspired by the song Relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired' looks like 'motivated' but means breathed in, a containment signal; 'Relax' is the 1983 hit by Frankie Goes to Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means evocative, calling something to mind.

clue.text: Monster pig discovered in westerly German city

indicators.note: in places the pig's middle inside the reversed city
westerly in an across clue means the word is read right to left

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so pig loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A monstrous pig is found in a German city in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' leaves I from PIG; 'westerly' turns ESSEN to NESSE, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loch Ness Monster of Scottish legend is known by this nickname.
